metadata.title: MPD-2047 planned land use versus satellite land cover (ESA WorldCover 2021), by MCD ward
metadata.satellite_source: ESA WorldCover 10 m 2021 v200, tile N27E075 (classification of Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery from 2021). (c) ESA WorldCover project, CC BY 4.0.
metadata.plan_source: Delhi Development Authority, Master Plan for Delhi 2047 GIS portal (gis.dda.org.in), via data/source/mpd2047_landuse_raw.geojson
metadata.method: Both layers are rasterised on the 10 m WorldCover grid and cross-tabulated inside each ward. Only pixels where the plan designates built, green/open or agricultural use are compared; the satellite shares are taken over those same pixels, so the two denominators match.

crosswalk_plan.not_compared: water (A2), monuments (P3), sports (P4), utilities (U, U1-U5) and blank codes

metadata.what_it_can_and_cannot_say: A satellite sees what is on the ground, not what the land is used for. The built-up group therefore lumps residential, industrial, commercial and public land together; the use_check section splits it only where OpenStreetMap has a land-use tag (residential and industrial are tagged fairly well, commercial and institutional poorly), and reports the untagged remainder as unknown. Trees inside residential colonies, parks with paved areas, fallow farmland and construction sites (bare) are classified as the satellite sees them. 10 m pixels, 2021 imagery, and the plan is from 2026: a plan-versus-satellite gap can be development that has not happened yet, change since 2021, or classifier error. It is not a measurement of compliance.
metadata.use_check_sources: OpenStreetMap land-use tags (data/delhi_landuse_simplified.geojson) where present; otherwise the DDA settlement layers (Lal Dora, PM-UDAY colonies, JJ clusters, from gis.dda.org.in, data/source/dda_settlements/); otherwise unknown. A DDA settlement counts as existing residential.
metadata.comparison_confidence_rule: ok when the comparable plan area is at least 0.15 km2 and the plan covers at least 10% of the ward

wards.comparison_confidence: low - thin coverage (small comparable plan area)
